product: A self-hosted n8n instance, reached with an owner-scoped API key
description: An agent holding an owner-scoped API key for a self-hosted workflow-automation platform, reaching it over its REST API and its MCP interface. The first grant on this site measured on a live instance rather than read from a page: a sandbox stood up for the exercise, with nothing else on it, probed on 13 September 2026 by an early beta user's agent. It built and ran a real AI-agent workflow against a real model credential, created and deleted one test workflow to measure create-change-delete and activation, and probed the edges — every account visible, an outbound node accepted with no restriction on target host, and credential metadata readable through one door and not through another. The rows are that write-up, translated row for row into the v0.3.0 vocabulary; where its barrier reading and the vocabulary's differ, the note says so.

reach_names.project: the workflows on the instance — the thing the key was given to build
reach_names.host: the instance itself: its accounts, its credential store, its execution records
reach_names.tenant: the platform as an account holder: activation, schedules, the model credential it spends against
reach_names.world: any host an outbound node can be pointed at — accepted on creation; what the platform's own server can reach was not tested

blocked.what: activating a workflow with no trigger, webhook or polling node
blocked.blocked_by: the platform's structural check on the workflow's shape, applied after the API has accepted the call
blocked.why: permitted by the API and rejected by the platform: a structural check on the workflow's shape, not on what it does once triggered
blocked.source: an independent measured check, 13 September 2026, run by an early beta user's agent against a sandbox instance stood up for the purpose; the write-up is held by RiskMandate

blocked.what: the credentials endpoint over the direct REST path — from the measuring environment
blocked.blocked_by: the measuring environment's own egress gateway, which intercepts any path naming credentials — a barrier in the investigator's environment, not the platform's
blocked.why: blocked before it reached the platform by the measuring environment's own egress gateway, which intercepts any path naming "credentials". A barrier in the investigator's environment, not the platform's; the same operation was open through the MCP interface
blocked.source: an independent measured check, 13 September 2026, run by an early beta user's agent against a sandbox instance stood up for the purpose; the write-up is held by RiskMandate

tools: the platform UI, by the deployer

grant.note: full create-change-delete confirmed: created, deactivated and deleted one real test workflow in the session. The write-up records the API key as "the technical gate — broad, but a real gate, not a prose rule"; in this vocabulary a key that permits a thing is the grant, not a barrier, so the row stands at none.

a webhook-triggered workflow was built, activated and executed. Activation is refused for a workflow with no trigger — a check on shape, not on risk — so the platform bounds nothing about what an activated workflow does.

via: REST API: an outbound-HTTP node on creation
grant.note: the API accepted a generic outbound-HTTP node pointed at an external URL with no restriction on target host; no allow-list observed. No workflow was executed against a non-public target, so what the platform's own server can reach on the network is not tested and is an open question below.

via: REST API: credentials (blocked at the investigator's gateway)
grant.note: the identical operation was blocked through the REST path — by the measuring environment's own gateway, not the platform — and returned full credential metadata through the MCP interface. Metadata only; nothing was exported. The write-up's own lesson: the barrier class of a capability can depend on which door was used to ask.
owner level on the account's personal project; the key was held for the session only and never persisted. Everything below it follows from it.

via: the AI Agent workflow, against a real model credential
grant.note: a real model credential was added by the deployer through the UI and a real execution returned a model response through the node — spend against that account, as the workflow's author. The first attempt failed with "does not have access to the credential": a wrong reference from ambiguous name matching between two credentials of the same type, not a barrier, found only once the MCP interface could list them.
execution records read: the zero-execution baseline, then the one real execution with its status and the model's response.
a workflow can carry a code node that runs on the platform's own server. Not tested in the session; derived from what the platform is, and an open question below.

not_in_grammar.what: see every account on the instance
not_in_grammar.permission: the owner-scoped key; no scoping beyond that observed
not_in_grammar.why: no primitive reads the user directory of a platform; the nearest, read.record.history, is a retained record, not a roster. Measured: a handful of accounts, one owner created the day of the session.
no primitive; measured as healthy, recorded for completeness

contradictions.advertised: the write-up classes the API key as a "setting" barrier — "the API key itself is the technical gate: broad, but a real gate, not a prose rule"
contradictions.permitted: in the v0.3.0 vocabulary a setting is "a switch the agent's own account can flip" and the enforcer test says a control bounds a grant only if enforced by something the grant does not include; the key is the grant, so every row it permits stands at none

contradictions.advertised: the platform's documented authorisation model: credential management is owner-level (from the write-up, "unconfirmed from outside")
contradictions.permitted: credential metadata was readable through the MCP interface; whether the same key can create, change or delete credentials was not tested

research_needed.question: What can the platform's own server reach on the network when a workflow runs? An outbound node was accepted on creation; none was executed against a non-public target.
research_needed.how: On a sandbox you are entitled to run, execute one workflow against an address the deployer names for the purpose; record the result and delete the workflow.

research_needed.question: Does a Code node on this instance run arbitrary code on the platform's server, and as which account?
research_needed.how: The platform's documentation for the Code node and its sandboxing settings, quoted; then one reversible probe on the sandbox.

research_needed.question: Beyond metadata: can the owner key create, change or delete credentials, and can it export a secret? The write-up stopped at metadata on purpose.
research_needed.how: The platform's public API reference for the credentials resource, quoted. Do not export a secret to find out.

research_needed.question: Should the measuring environment's gateway rule (block any path naming "credentials") be extended to MCP-tunnelled requests, now that the bypass is confirmed? A decision for the deployer.
research_needed.how: The deployer decides; record the decision in the vault's history.
